messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Leisure, tourism and sport and Youth in Germany during the 1960s, matching this research need: data on youth leisure clubhouses and their effects on adolescents’ leisure activities, friendships, family life, and personal development, including parent and youth surveys with social attitudes, club participation, housing, education, and socioeconomic background
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS Daten Jugendfreizeitheim 1960 Eltern Jugendliche Befragung Freizeitheim
1960s Germany youth leisure clubhouses parents survey youth archive dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Social Structure of German Sport Youth (Sozialstruktur der deutschen Sportjugend), 1958 — GESIS ZA0234","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0234","justification":"Highly relevant historical dataset examining leisure activities, social relationships, personal development, and family influences among young people in West Germany. Surveyed 1,879 sports club members aged 15–25 in 1958, providing a close pre-1960s comparison. Variables include club membership duration, leisure and sporting activities, parental influence on leisure organization, upbringing, socialization, educational and occupational circumstances, cultural interests, relationships with older generations, religious attitudes, and social integration. Particularly useful for investigating how organized youth activities shaped adolescents' friendships, identities, social attitudes, and development. Does not specifically evaluate youth leisure clubhouses or include a separate parent survey."},{"title":"Youth Leisure Activities in the GDR, 1969 (Freizeitverhalten Jugendlicher) — GESIS ZA6036","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.6036","justification":"Relevant late-1960s East German research dataset examining young people's leisure activities and interests. Associated research documentation includes studies of leisure behavior according to parents' occupational groups, parental socioeconomic influences, cultural participation, and the relationship between education and leisure. Particularly useful for exploring how family background and social circumstances influenced adolescents' recreational choices during the 1960s. Provides historical context for youth leisure participation in East Germany, although direct measures of clubhouse effects and parent-youth comparisons require verification in the documentation."},{"title":"Leisure in the Ruhr Area, 1970 (Freizeit im Ruhrgebiet 1970) — GESIS ZA0649","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0649","justification":"Closely related to the research topic because it explicitly measures leisure activities taking place in clubhouses, residential neighborhoods, and private homes. Conducted in May–June 1970 in West Germany's Ruhr region, immediately after the target decade. Variables include preferred leisure pursuits, frequency of activities in clubhouses, opportunities for recreation near home, obstacles to leisure participation, organized sporting activities, sports club membership, and preferences for leisure facilities. Useful for investigating the relationship between recreational infrastructure, housing environments, and participation in organized leisure. The survey covers the broader population rather than exclusively adolescents."},{"title":"Youth Welfare Survey, Offenbach District, 1980 (Jugendhilfe-Untersuchung, Kreis Offenbach) — GESIS ZA1258","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.1258","justification":"Exceptionally close thematic match, although conducted in 1980 rather than the 1960s. Surveyed approximately 3,080 young people aged 12–22 in the Offenbach district of West Germany. Covers leisure activities, friendship networks, frequency and location of recreational activities, club membership and participation, boredom, housing conditions, access to personal rooms, neighborhood environments, family relationships, parenting experiences, household composition, and shared family activities. Particularly valuable for examining relationships between youth leisure participation, friendships, family life, housing, and personal development. Could provide a comparative framework for analyzing earlier youth clubhouse programs, but cannot directly establish their effects during the 1960s."}]}
